notes:
First example of [3,12] = Z/3 x Z/12 for a geometrically simple genus 2 Jacobian over Q (previously known only for Jacobians split over Q).

Output of pipeline/magma/prepare_submission.m (Magma V2.29-4): J(Q)_tors = [3,12]; gcd of #J(F_p) over 25 good primes = 36 (sharp); strict prime 37, chi = x^4 - x^3 - 37*x + 1369. Independent PARI/GP check (hyperellcharpoly): gcd 36 over 71 good odd p < 400, 16 strict primes below 200. Sage/Lombardo: End(J_Qbar) = Z. #Aut(C) = 2. Conductor: the odd part is 3^5*5^2*7^2*17*47 (PARI genus2red); the exponent at 2 is not computed.

How it was found: by a sieve over the order-12 chart A(12), written in coordinates (A,z,B) = (p^2, z, p*r). The sieve kept points with Frobenius polynomial = (x-1)^2 (x-p)^2 mod 3 and 36 | #J(F_p) at good primes. The curve is at (A,z,B) = (-2/3, 5, -10). On the line (A,B) = (-2/3,-10), the extra rational 3-torsion point exists exactly over the rational points of the rank-1 elliptic curve w^2 = (3z^2+25)(3z^2+121) (conductor 990). This gives infinitely many geometrically simple Jacobians with torsion exactly [3,12] (a computational proof, independently re-verified). Six further non-isomorphic simple [3,12] curves were found.
